blocks.text: # Results matrix — qualified STALE Phase 1 and archived mechanism records
## Supersession notice

The valid 80-scenario STALE Phase 1 Nano qualification below remains the predeclared primary result. Two independent Gemini judge passes on the same frozen answers did not reproduce its P3−P2 gain, so the combined evidence is judge-sensitive rather than a robust mechanism effect. Neither result authorizes a 400-scenario run. Historic MemConflict, Harvey, C&H, transport attempts, and technical-invalid STALE inventories are never pooled with it.
## Completed Matrix F: STALE / CUPMem Phase 1 Nano qualification

The sole valid matrix root is `/Users/richardtang/.cache/proofpress-eval/phase1-stale-v2/2026-08-08-nano-gateway-qualification-inventory-gated`, bound to the 80-carrier frozen admission inventory. Every selected UID has completed, telemetry-eligible V0/V1/P2/P3 records; P2/P3 verified semantic and prompt-token parity; and arm-blinded official scoring through OpenRouter using `openai/gpt-5.4-nano`. No v17–v20 record or other historical inventory is included.

The paired primary estimate is `P3 − P2 = +8.33pp` across 80 shared eligible scenarios, with a scenario-clustered 95% CI of `[+1.25pp, +15.42pp]`; 30 scenarios improved, 38 tied, and 12 regressed. The predeclared Luna gate passed. `V1 − V0 = +60.83pp` is a calibration/reproduction contrast, not a provenance-only estimate. P3 does not beat V1 and is not intended to: V1 has full-session CUPMem write-time adjudication and conflict-aware readout, whereas P2/P3 test a portable successor handoff.

The Nano-only claim was narrow: with non-provenance semantic content held equal between P2 and P3, admitted status, lineage, integrity, and the minimal inspect policy improved task behavior in this STALE slice, mainly by reducing unsupported inheritance. The two independent Gemini judge passes below did not reproduce that effect. The result therefore does not establish a judge-robust mechanism effect, generalization, replacement for shared memory, or an independent head-to-head product victory over CUPMem. The next evidence must be scorer-disagreement/failure analysis plus an information-matched shared-memory control and independent artifact-revision handoff work; no 400-scenario run begins automatically.
## Secondary Matrix F-R: blinded Gemini judge robustness replication

The same four frozen, arm-blinded answer exports were rescored without rerunning any task, carrier, or admission step. `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` was called through the direct Gemini API using `GEMINI_API_KEY`, the official evaluator's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and concurrency 2; all 320 judged scenarios completed with zero judge errors. Inputs, score hashes, and the paired analysis are bound in `official_scores/gemini-3.5-flash-lite/replication-manifest.json` under the immutable matrix root.

Across the same 80 shared eligible scenarios, Gemini gives paired `P3 − P2 = −1.67pp`, scenario-clustered 95% CI `[−7.50pp, +4.17pp]`; its gate does not pass. This is a secondary robustness result, not a replacement or a pooled estimate for the predeclared Nano outcome. It makes the honest current conclusion: the STALE result is sensitive to the LLM judge, so no judge-independent treatment-effect claim is yet warranted.
### Same-model Gemini repeat

An independent second pass by the same `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` judge, with the same frozen arm-blinded inputs and concurrency 2, also completed 320/320 scenarios with zero judge errors. It scored `P3 − P2 = −2.08pp`, scenario-clustered 95% CI `[−8.33pp, +4.17pp]`;  its gate did not pass. The per-criterion results were State Resolution 30.00% P3 versus 46.25% P2, Premise Resistance 13.75% versus 5.00%, and Implicit Policy Adaptation 26.25% versus 25.00%; overall P3 was 56/240 (23.33%) versus P2 61/240 (25.42%).

Across the two Gemini passes, agreement across each arm's 240 criterion decisions was 95.83% for V0, 94.58% for V1, 95.42% for P2, and 91.67% for P3. This repeat establishes that the Gemini null/negative direction is not a single-pass fluctuation, but the two passes share the same answers and judge family, so they are not pooled or treated as additional independent task scenarios. Raw outputs, hashes, and the agreement analysis are at `official_scores/gemini-3.5-flash-lite-repeat-2/` under the immutable matrix root.
## Scorer-disagreement audit: abstention-policy confound

The frozen-answer audit aligned all 960 arm-by-criterion decisions from Nano with both Gemini passes; it did not rerun a target agent, carrier, or judge. Gemini repeated itself on 906/960 decisions (94.38%), while both Gemini passes jointly disagreed with Nano on 224/960. The concentrated disagreements are in the portable arms' State Resolution criterion: P2 has 36/80 Nano-versus-Gemini-consensus disagreements (22 contain an abstention cue), and P3 has 43/80 (all 43 contain an abstention cue). The corresponding Gemini repeat agreement is 75/80 for P2 and 72/80 for P3.

The official Dim 1 rubric says to fail a response that “claims ignorance.” In the reviewed disagreement traces, Nano treats a carrier-grounded “I cannot determine; abstain/re-verify” as correctly refusing to assume `M_old`; both Gemini passes fail it precisely because it abstains instead of declaring the new state. This is not evidence that either judge has established ground truth. It identifies a measurement-policy ambiguity: the P3 carrier's intended safe behavior is entangled with the judge's treatment of abstention, so the observed P3−P2 contrast is not presently separable into a provenance effect alone.

At the criterion level Nano has 39 P3 gains, 182 ties, and 19 P3 losses; Gemini pass 1 has 21/194/25 and pass 2 has 24/187/29. Where both Gemini passes agree, 30 Nano P3 gains become Gemini ties, 2 become Gemini P3 losses, and 20 Nano ties become Gemini P3 losses. A deterministic 24-case arm-blinded adjudication packet and a separate deblinding key are preserved with `disagreement-summary.json` at `official_scores/scorer-disagreement-audit/` under the immutable root. An independent rubric adjudication must choose how safe abstention scores before selecting a judge or authorizing any scale-up.
## What the paper must distinguish
The study has three different questions. They should not be collapsed into one leaderboard number.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  A["Does provenance reduce stale-authority use?\nMemConflict"] --> B["Does it help at enterprise corpus scale?\nC&H"]
  B --> C["Does the effect transfer across professional work?\nAPEX"]
```
## Completed Matrix E: MemConflict mechanism gate

This internal fixture is a historical mechanism check, not the first phase of the active research plan. It is deliberately reported separately from STALE, Harvey, C&H, APEX, and any Gateway qualification because its local Codex runner did not record resolved provider, Gateway cost, or fallback telemetry.

| Arm | Runs | Trusted success | Task success | Stale/regression | Correct reversal |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `baseline_continuous` | 24 | 62.5% | 75.0% | 12.5% | 75.0% |
| `ordinary_memory` | 24 | 83.3% | 95.8% | 12.5% | 95.8% |
| `proofpress_provenance` | 24 | 83.3% | 87.5% | 4.2% | 87.5% |

The primary Provenance−Memory contrast is 0.0 points on trusted success, −8.3 points on task success, and −8.3 points on stale/regression rate. Gate A passed and Gate B failed. The defensible interpretation is a small stale-authority signal without a quality gain; the study must preserve this null result and inspect scorer/answer-normalization behavior before any scale-up.
## Completed Matrix A: isolated external-handoff diagnostic
This is a single-edge experiment. The upstream artifact and public workspace are identical; only the materialized history changes.

| Dimension | Fixed | Varied |
|---|---|---|
| Task | 2 frozen Harvey tasks | task instance |
| Handoff boundary | `V1 → V2`, `V2 → V3` | boundary |
| Upstream content | canonical evidence map / decision register | never varies inside a pair |
| Receiver | fresh session, same role, same M0 model and effort | three independent attempts |
| Arm | same current artifact and token budget | `mas-memory`, `mas-proofpress-lineage` |

Completed cells: `2 tasks × 2 boundaries × 2 arms × 3 attempts = 24` receiver-only calls per tested model. The recorded DeepSeek 0731, Muse Spark 1.2, and GPT-5.6 Luna slices completed their receiver-call integrity checks. This validates the transport path; it is not a native Proofpress outcome score.

Primary measurements: decision recovery accuracy, decision regression, unsupported authority upgrade, correct reversal, false block, input tokens, latency, tool calls/history reads. Its value is causal clarity: if Proofpress changes an outcome here, the difference cannot be blamed on upstream agents having produced different artifacts.
## Completed Matrix B: archived external-transport end-to-end prototype

This was a preliminary systems experiment, not the final product-form experiment. It compared `memory.md`/`handoff.log` with an external `provenance.md`; that is now classified as a transport prototype.

| Observed model | Ordinary memory criterion success | External Proofpress sidecar criterion success | Interpretation |
|---|---:|---|
| DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 | 297/375 (79.2%) | 294/375 (78.4%) | near-flat; lowest-cost stable candidate |
| Muse Spark 1.2 | 328/375 (87.5%) | 290/375 (77.3%) | not interpretable as native effect; one treatment workflow had empty final output |
| GPT-5.6 Luna | 288/375 (76.8%) | 296/375 (78.9%) | near-flat/slightly positive sidecar result |

Across 36 workflows, the Harvey all-pass endpoint was 0/36. Harvey requires every criterion to pass, so this difficult-task endpoint is retained as a secondary hardness diagnostic. The 1,125 per-arm criterion opportunities are the descriptive quality signal, but must be reported by task and model rather than only pooled.

All 36 workflow records completed their five stages, 35/36 had nonempty final outputs, and the sole empty final output occurred in the Muse external-Proofpress cell. This exposed a V4 final-output preflight gap. Three Muse route-metadata events were unresolved; DeepSeek recorded 1,076/1,076 resolved DeepInfra events. These operational facts are not treatment-quality outcomes.
For each cell, report:

| Quality | Trust | Efficiency | Integrity |
|---|---|---|---|
| official Harvey rubric and `trusted_task_success` | regression, unsupported upgrade, correct reversal, false block | input/output tokens, latency, cost, tools, history reads | capsule verification, artifact continuity, declared actor/status agreement |

## Accepted Matrix D: Gateway Harvey B0 and SAS follow-up

The historical Gateway PSA slice `gateway-0731-harvey-psa-c0-c3-qualification-v1` stopped and is **not qualified**. Its Chat Completions C0 run recorded 37 calls and `$0.093275` actual Gateway cost, but returned unversioned Flash without provider/fallback routing metadata; its record remains immutable operational history. The current native AI SDK v4 adapter is separately frozen for B0 one-shot and C0/C3 SAS slices, requiring exact 0731 model, actual provider, routing/fallback metadata, and numeric `usage.cost` per call. B0 never enters the C0/C3 slice-level qualification verdict, and neither qualification is a treatment-effect analysis.

The GLM and Gemini PSA qualification slices are complete but unqualified operational history. Luna/Terra v1 is immutable pre-inference history. V2 plus independent scorer-extension roots completed all three B0/C0/C3 executions and all nine 75-criterion score cells with exact OpenAI resolution, no fallback, complete telemetry, preflight, and C3 lineage. The final PSA-only criterion rates are B0 66/75, 66/75, 66/75; C0 64/75, 67/75, 67/75; C3 65/75, 65/75, 65/75. `C0−B0` and `C3−C0` are reported as paired descriptive contrasts below; `C3−B0` remains mixed and cannot be attributed to Proofpress.

| Arm | Tasks | Attempts | Primary role |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `B0 harvey-one-shot` | 2 | 3 | original Harvey continuous-session baseline |
| `C0 sas-ordinary` | 2 | 3 | five-stage fresh-session SAS ordinary-continuity control |
| `C3 sas-proofpress` | 2 | 3 | same SAS flow plus admitted Proofpress lineage and independent verification |

`C0 − B0` is the fresh-session SAS/sessionization comparison. The primary Proofpress estimate is paired `C3 − C0`, reported by task and never pooled with archived transport data. `C3 − B0` is a mixed total difference and cannot be interpreted as a Proofpress effect. Every Gateway call must retain requested/resolved model, actual provider, `usage.cost`, fallback status/metadata, tokens, and latency. Missing telemetry makes a workflow audit-visible but ineligible for the formal matrix; wrapper-local `$0` is not an observed cost. STATE-Bench, MemConflict, HiEviDR-Bench, and DeepResearch Bench follow only as independently frozen/reported slices, with the latter two requiring adapter/scorer gates first.

## Interpretation rules

| Observed pattern | Responsible statement |
|---|---|
| Proofpress improves isolated recovery and end-to-end trusted success versus strong memory, without reversal harm | Evidence supports a bounded provenance-handoff mechanism for the frozen tasks/workflow/model(s). |
| Proofpress wins only against latest artifact, not strong memory | Claim ordinary handoff memory matters; do not claim a distinctive Proofpress benefit. |
| Proofpress matches memory but uses fewer tokens/latency/history reads | Claim an efficiency or auditability advantage only if task/trust quality is not materially worse. |
| Proofpress is worse at justified reversal or causes false blocks | The preservation framing failed on adaptive decision-making; report it and revise the protocol. |
| Effect appears only in one model team | State a model interaction, not a general provenance effect. |
| Controls lack the intended recovery error | Stop or redesign; a scaled matrix would not test the proposed mechanism. |
## What is not a valid conclusion

- A higher Harvey rubric alone does not prove preserved trust.
- A model sweep does not compare harnesses.
- A raw-history win does not imply that more context is intrinsically better; it may only expose a missing ordinary-memory control.
- An ARA trace or a valid Proofpress capsule does not certify legal correctness; it records research/artifact provenance at different layers.
## Archived APEX official-runner qualification and Law task-fit pilot

This is an **APEX official-runner qualification record**, not an official APEX leaderboard score and not a Proofpress efficacy result. The pinned Archipelago checkout used Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview for both the agent and native grader; the task/world/MCP/system prompt and native grader were otherwise unchanged, apart from the disclosed Docker build-compatibility repair. A direct Gemini tool-call canary passed before the runs.

The Investment Banking task `task_3e2e533b49374381acf2056fe479e3ba` produced four valid completed Gemini runs, each with native score `0/5`. This is not a grader failure: the native rubric reads the final deck and checks the five target enterprise values implied by the unrounded peer median (about `24.18x`). The agent instead selected rounded-display values of `24.3x` or `24.6x`, yielding consistently incorrect enterprise values. A fifth launch stalled in a provider call, was stopped at user direction, and is recorded as an `infrastructure_abort` with no trajectory or grades; it is excluded from the four completed qualifications and from all score denominators. Finance is now archived: it is a single-agent source-authority/modeling task with a floor effect, not an artifact-handoff efficacy substrate.

The Law task `task_323b4e29af5e4c7f86eaf4a24c4487ad` is a better revision-shaped candidate. Its completed Gemini pilot scored `4/6`: the redraft correctly established the lessee as signatory, lessee certifications/warranties, no early termination option, and 0.73 Additional Rent share; it failed to replace `Tenant` with `Lessee` and `Landlord` with `Lessor` consistently. The task therefore has a persistent source artifact, a revision deliverable, and six native rubrics. But its lease, correspondence, and prior certificate are all available to a fresh Agent B in a clean world. It is consequently a Law negative-control/calibration track unless the derived two-stage boundary is kept to Agent A's private review work rather than falsely claiming that provenance supplied inaccessible source facts.
### Archived APEX-derived Law Artifact Handoff Track (public-source negative control, 3+3)

The calibration run at `/private/tmp/proofpress-apex-law-calibration-20260809/run-3x3-v10` completed all 6/6 receivers with the pinned Archipelago commit `1c3dcd4694b313020cd626699c9c7cc1c0a2fc58`, task/world `task_323b4e29af5e4c7f86eaf4a24c4487ad` / `world_eec3883ca3c54c41a62d3f220a27736c`, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview through Vercel AI Gateway, 300-second per-call timeout, 3,900-second watchdog, and native Gemini grading of the final snapshot. It is an **APEX-derived Artifact Handoff Track**, never an official APEX score.

| Pair | Upstream native | Ordinary native / audit | Proofpress native / audit | Pair interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 4/6 | 4/6, 3/7 | 4/6, 3/7 | equal residual terminology/revision errors |
| 2 | 4/6 | 6/6, 7/7 | 6/6, 7/7 | both arms fully repaired the artifact |
| 3 | 2/6 | 4/6, 5/7 | 4/6, 5/7 | both arms repaired two rubric failures |

The arms are exactly tied: native pass rate `14/18` (`77.8%`) each and audit pass rate `15/21` (`71.4%`) each. All three Proofpress capsules passed independent verification; ordinary packages had semantic parity with their paired Proofpress package and `not_applicable` capsule verification. There were no v10 infrastructure/model aborts; two ordinary-receiver Gateway connection errors were retried successfully. This null calibration validates execution and integrity instrumentation but supplies no efficacy claim, because the task exposes all underlying sources to a fresh receiver and the sample is only 3+3. It remains an archived public-source negative control: it is not a full-access cell for the next track, cannot identify an access-condition interaction, and must not be reinterpreted as a restricted-access result.
### Planned APEX-derived Restricted-Access Artifact Handoff Track

| Status | Estimand | Receiver isolation | Blind scoring and expansion gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| planned; not yet scored | `Proofpress − ordinary` conditional on the same semantic handoff and restricted source access | fresh receiver snapshot permits only current artifact plus memory/log/handoff; all original source documents, archives, app data, Agent A trajectory, and scratchpad are denied and leakage-tested | native judge receives only a neutral final-DOCX package; independent seven-cell audit is arm-blind; a 1+1 boundary pilot must pass before serial randomized 3+3 |

The ordinary arm is a conventional readable artifact plus memory/log/handoff. Proofpress carries the same semantic content with native anchors, admitted head, declared decision lineage, and a capsule. The capsule verifies the package's identity, integrity, and declared lineage; it does not verify the truth of inaccessible source evidence. This is a cross-boundary/cross-world condition, not a cross-system interoperability claim. The Lease narrative is an access discontinuity such as an external VDR closing or access being revoked while the organization retains its records. Only an observed ordinary error space, pairwise semantic and draft-hash parity, no source leakage, arm-blind grading, and a Proofpress improvement or non-regression in trusted success justify expansion to another task.
